articleTitle: A Ku-band Miniaturized LNA in 0.18-µm CMOS Process for Low-cost Phased Array Application
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A Ku-band miniaturized CMOS low noise amplifier (LNA) for phased array application has been implemented using 0.18-µm RF CMOS technology. The methods for performance and biasing optimization under size constraint are proposed to obtain good overall performance tradeoffs while maintaining miniaturization. In the first stage, capacitor cross-coupled differential structure is utilized to realize gm enhancement, partial noise cancellation, and bandwidth extension. In the second stage, differential cascode transistors with current mirror circuit are employed to alleviate the impact of process fluctuations and temperature variation. Under a 1.8 V supply voltage, the Ku-band CMOS LNA provides a minimum noise figure of 4.5 dB at 17 GHz and a highest power gain of 16.8 dB at 17.5 GHz in measurement.

articleTitle: A Flexible Low-Cost Hybrid Beamforming Structure for Practical Beamforming Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, a simplified yet flexible half-duplex hybrid beamforming (HBF) architecture along with the adaptive beam scanning and direction-finding methodology for the 360° HBF system has been proposed. The structure is constructed using up to 4 units of n × 4 antenna arrays with choice of gain and coverage sector, which is powered by only 4 RF beamforming chains. In addition, the flexible beamforming structure is able to enable beamforming function of any legacy transceiver. The proposed architecture exhibits prominent advantages in reducing the hardware complexity and cost of the HBF system by 4 folds and offers the field-friendly feature with the flexible gain and coverage concept that allow only the necessary array to be installed.

articleTitle: 30-GHz Co-designed Low-Noise Amplifier and Antenna-on-Chip for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents a 30-GHz co-design of a 28-dB high-gain low-noise amplifier (LNA) and a 54% high-efficiency monopole antenna-on-chip for 5G wireless applications. The LNA design is based on a two-stage differential cascode structure with inductive degeneration. The antenna design is a modified monopole structure to maximize the radiation efficiency. Both parts are integrated directly on the same silicon chip in a 0.25 µm SiGe BiCMOS technology. A co-design method is proposed according to various considerations and a compact matching network is implemented to achieve the optimal power and noise matching. The measurement results show a total gain of 27 dB of the complete system.

articleTitle: A K-Band Low-Loss High-Isolation CMOS SPDT Switch Based on Multi-Tap Inductor Technique
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A K-band single-pole double-throw (SPDT) transmit/receive (T/R) switch is presented in this paper. To improve bandwidth while decreasing chip area, the switch is designed using multi-tap inductor together with capacitors that replaces the λ/4 transmission line. It achieves a measured minimum insertion loss of 1.62 dB at 21 GHz, with an isolation of 24 dB. Measured output port to port isolation is better than 22 dB. The return losses at all ports are better than 10 dB from 14 to 28 GHz with a P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1dB</sub> of 8 dBm. It is fabricated in 65 nm CMOS and occupies a core chip area of 0.035 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A Compact 38-54 GHz Sub-Harmonic Mixer with Improved Linearity in 65-nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents a 38-54 GHz sub-harmonic up-conversion mixer in 65 nm CMOS process using derivative superposition third-order transconductance cancellation technique. The measurement results demonstrate -2.5 dB conversion gain and -11.7 dBm OP1dB at IF input frequency of 100 MHz and RF frequency of 41 GHz with relatively low power. The 3-dB RF bandwidth covers 38 to 54 GHz. The dc power consumption of the mixer is 8.5 mW. The improvement of OIP3 is 4 dB (from 0 to 4 dBm). The chip area of the proposed mixer is 0.8 × 0.55 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Large Signal Behavioral Modeling of Power Transistor from Active Load-pull Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Large signal behavioral modeling for RF power transistor has been developed rapidly in the past decade, this paper compares and contrasts recent nonlinear large-signal behavioral modeling techniques designed for power transistors. These techniques include traditional function based behavioral modeling techniques, e.g. X-parameters, Padé model, Cardiff model, load-pull X-parameters; and artificial neural network (ANN) and machine learning (ML) technique based methods, e.g. real value feed-forward neural network (RVFFNN) model, Bayesian inference model, support vector regression (SVR) based model, in the frequency domains. Besides, approaches to generating the data for modeling from active load-pull measurements are reviewed as well, including closed loop, feed-forward, and open loop active load pull system.

articleTitle: Low-loss Substrate Material for Millimeter-wave and THz Applications (Invited)
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: The development of a new type of low dielectric loss, flexible and optically transparent substrate material-cyclic olefin copolymer (COC) for millimeter-wave and terahertz (THz) applications is reported in this paper. In the past, COC material was mainly used in applications of medical devices, detection instruments, lens, optical films, etc. By using a novel thermal control method, COC material with a new ratio of norbornene to ethylene has been fabricated into COC substrates with various thickness successfully. The COC substrates were measured in millimeter-wave and THz bands, and the results show that the COC dissipation factor is lower than that of the widely used RT 5880 and quartz.

articleTitle: A Wideband W-Band Driver Amplifier in 0.1 μm GaAs Process
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband low ripple W-band driver amplifier in 0.1 μm GaAs Process. The proposed amplifier consists of four common-source stages. In the amplifier, the matching network and system stability, which is important to the amplifier performance, are analyzed. Measured gain shows a peak gain of 19.2 dB at 99 GHz with a relative 3-dB bandwidth of 42% (from 67 GHz to 103 GHz). The input and output return losses are better than 6 dB and 8 dB, respectively. The saturated output power (Psat) is greater than 14 dBm in the 3-dB bandwidth frequency range with a peak value of 17.1 dBm at 100 GHz. The amplifier consumes the power of 297 mW with a supply voltage of 3.3 V and an area of 1.3 × 0.7 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Multi-bias Small Signal Circuit Model for FinFET Transistors
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, a multi-bias small signal circuit model for Fin Field-Effect transistor (FinFET) is proposed. Channel length modulation effect, non-quasi-static effect and the loss and coupling effects of the substrate are considered in this model. For verification, silicon Multi-Fin MOSFET was fabricated in 14 nm bulk FinFET technology. Based on the improved open/short deembedding method and the proposed model, the scattering parameters calculated by the model are compared with the measurement results. The magnitude root-mean-square-error (RMSE) of scattering parameter is less than 0.0082 for the proposed small signal circuit model. The comparison result indicates that the proposed model achieves high accuracy from 0.2 GHz to 50.2 GHz.

Index Terms: Root Mean Square Error Of Model

articleTitle: Design and Modeling of Millimeter-Wave Transformer in Silicon: A Tutorial (Invited)
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A comprehensive review of transformer design and modeling techniques in silicon technology is presented in this paper. Compact, distributed and coupled T-line models of the transformer are established and compared in terms of common-mode and differential-mode behaviors. By use of the modeling technique, the bandwidth and the insertion loss of weakly- and strongly-coupled transformers are explored, and corresponding design examples are provided.

articleTitle: A 78-93 GHz Power Amplifier with 19.6-dBm Psat and 12.8 % PAEpeak in 0.1-µm GaAs pHEMT for Radio Astronomical Receiver System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A W-band power amplifier (PA) for radio astronomical receiver LO chain in 0.1-μm GaAs pHEMT technology is presented in this paper. This PA is a 3-stage common source design using transmission lines to implement matching network. In order to increase the bandwidth, two sections matching networks for output are utilized to maintain the matching loci within the Q = 1 contour of Smith chart. A 90 degrees Lange coupler is employed to enhance the bandwidth and to combine the output power. The chip size with all pads is 2×1.5 mm2. From the measurement results, the proposed PA achieves 11.5-dB small signal gain with 15-GHz 3-dB bandwidth (78-93 GHz), saturated output power (P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sat</sub>) of 19.6 dBm, output 1-dB compression point (OP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1dB</sub>) of 18.2 dBm, and maximum power added efficiency (PAE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">peak</sub>) of 12.8%.

articleTitle: High-Selectivity Bandpass Filter With Wide Upper Stopband Using Harmonic Suppression Structure
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A high-selectivity bandpass filter (BPF) with ultra-wide upper stopband is proposed in this paper. Four cross-coupled microstrip slow-wave open-loop resonators are utilized to implement a filtering response with high selectivity. To extend its stopband bandwidth, the folded stepped-impedance microstrip line with open stubs is introduced to suppress the harmonics. By cascading these two parts, a high selectivity BPF with wide stopband can be achieved. To verify the aforementioned mechanisms, the proposed BPF is implemented, fabricated, and measured. The attenuation slope of 168.6 dB/GHz and 265.3 dB/GHz in the lower and upper side of passbands is measured. Meanwhile, this filter can generate an ultra-wide upper stopband up to 25 GHz with rejection level larger than 24.2 dB.

Author Keywords: folded stepped-impedance microstrip line with open stubs

articleTitle: A D-band Balanced Frequency Doubler with Marchand Balun Structure
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A D-band broadband frequency doubler based on a 65-nm CMOS technology is proposed in this paper. This doubler with an output frequency of 110~170GHz is implemented by a single-balanced topology based on Marchand balun. When the input power is 10dBm, the conversion gain of the frequency doubler is -13dB to -10dB, the fundamental suppression is greater than 19dB, and the 3-dB bandwidth is 50%. The chip size including all pads is 0.45*0.58 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Dual-Feedback GaN HEMT Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper designs a low-phase noise 5.2 GHz GaN HEMT oscillator with GaN-on-SiC HEMT foundry process of WIN semiconductors. The oscillator uses a dual-feedback technique, the first feedback uses a transformer coupling feedback and the second feedback uses a low-pass π-filter feedback. The GaN oscillator uses buffer to characterize the oscillator performance. At the power 14.9 mW the oscillator generates a signal at 5.2 GHz. At 1MHz frequency offset from the carrier at 5.2 GHz the phase noise is -125.77 dBc/Hz, the figure of merit (FoM) of the proposed oscillator is -188 dBc/Hz. The dualfeedback oscillator uses a chip size of 2×1 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A 94-GHz Push-Push Frequency Doubler with Peak Total Power Efficiency of 16.28%
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A highly efficient 94-GHz push-push frequency doubler is presented. The push-push frequency doubler is implemented with a commercial 65-nm CMOS process and can be operated in high-power mode (HPM) and high-efficiency mode (HEM). In HPM, it shows peak conversion gain of 1.94 dB, operating in the frequency range from 83.6 to 102.9 GHz (20.7%) with the input power of -1 dBm within 3-dB gain variation. Also at 94 GHz, it operates in the input power range of -11.9 to 8 dBm within 3-dB gain variation. In HEM, the peak total efficiency (P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OUT</sub>/(P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DC</sub> + P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">IN</sub>)) is 16.28%, which is the highest among those of the reported W-Band frequency doublers.

articleTitle: Propagation Characteristics of A 2.4GHz Wireless Sensor Module with A Pattern Antenna in Forestry and Agriculture Field
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper describes 2.4 GHz RF peer-to-peer propagation measurements and modeling in forests and a Japonica paddy field. Propagation through vegetation is an important subject for creating a reliable wireless sensor network system. Detailed measurement curves of RSSI (received signal strength indication) against distance indicate the presence of various vegetation types based on the moisture conditions of plants. The SRET (simplified radiative energy transfer-based model fits well depending on leaf density for NLOS (non-line-of-sight) conditions in the forests and the paddy field. In the case of LOS (line-of-sight) conditions of paddy field, a novel model named the "TRPF (two-ray paddy field) model" is proposed in order to express the influence of vegetation for a reflection wave.

articleTitle: Iteration Process Analysis of Real-Valued Time-Delay Neural Network with Different Activation Functions for Power Amplifier Behavioral Modeling
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: The dynamic iteration process analysis of real-valued time-delay neural network (RVTDNN) for power amplifier (PA) behavioral modeling is provided in this paper. The performance with three activation functions of hyperbolic tangent sigmoid (tansig), logistic sigmoid (logsig) and rectified linear unit (ReLU) are investigated. It is discovered that RVTDNN with ReLU has the fastest convergence speed, and the ones with tansig and logsig have similar modeling accuracy which is higher than ReLU, but slower convergence speed, validated by experiments on a Doherty PA. The iteration process investigation of RVTDNN with different activation functions provides practical considerations for applying the model into different future 5G scenarios.

articleTitle: A Wideband W-band 6-bit Active Phase Shifter in 28-nm RF CMOS
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A wideband W-band 6-bit vector-sum based active phase shifter which was implemented using a 28-nm RF CMOS process is presented. The proposed phase shifter consists of a differential I/Q generator and a vector-summing amplifier with differential input and output buffers to use virtual grounds at high frequencies. The I/Q generator was designed with a differential hybrid coupler structure, and the mismatch in its differential input should be small to obtain accurate I/Q signals. To reduce the differential mismatch at the I/Q generator input, source cross-coupling capacitors are introduced at the common-gate stage of the cascode input buffer. The measured results indicate a root mean square (RMS) gain error of 0.69-0.98 dB and RMS phase error of 6.8-9.3 degrees over a wide frequency range of 76 GHz to 104 GHz. The average peak gain of all 64 states is 3.5 dB at 82 GHz. The fabricated phase shifter has a chip area of 0.32 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> with power consumption of 26 mW.

articleTitle: A K-Band High-Gain LNA in 0.13-µm RF CMOS
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents a K-band low-noise amplifier (LNA) for automotive radar applications. The LNA features high gain and low noise using a 3-stage cascode topology, which has been designed in a 0.13-μm RF CMOS. According to the measurement results, the maximum gain is 31.2 dB at 24 GHz and the -3-dB bandwidth has 1.7 GHz from 23.8 to 25.5 GHz. The NF achieves 4.9 dB at 24.5 GHz. The input and output return losses S11 and S22 at 24 GHz are -13.5 dB and -10.5 dB, respectively. The total power consumption is 22.3 mW at a supply of 1.5 V. The chip occupies a whole area of 0.93×0.57 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A Coupling and Decoupling Device for Pulsed Current Injection in MIL-STD-188-125-2
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In order to implement kA level pulsed current injection (PCI) in MIL-STD-188-125-2, a coupling circuit composed of the varistor and a decoupling circuit based on ferrite cores are designed by circuit analysis and simulation. Afterwards, the two parts were integrated into a compact device and validated in a PCI test. The validation result shows that the device can provide a high coupling and decoupling efficiency for kA level PCI, meanwhile does not interfere with normal operation of equipment under test. The device can be used to test the performance of electrical point-of-entry (POE) protective devices and long-line protection modules (LLPMs) for high-altitude electromagnetic pulse.

articleTitle: A K To Ka Band Single-ended To Balanced Ultra-wideband LNA In 45nm CMOS SOI
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, a K to Ka band single-ended to balanced ultra-wideband low noise amplifier (LNA) is presented. By employing shunt feedback network, the LNA circuit can achieve a better wideband performance. On the other hand, adding another transistor in the first-stage circuit to invert the signal, the LNA circuit can operate at a differential mode while maintaining a single-ended signal input. In addition, a capacitance cross coupling network is introduced to solve the problem of signal amplitude inconsistency. Using a standard 45nm SOI CMOS process, the proposed LNA exhibits 23 dB gain and a noise figure of 2.7 dB to 3.2 dB from 18 to 40 GHz, while the input and output return loss are less than 10 dB, respectively.

articleTitle: On-Chip Inductor for Millimeter-wave Regime
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: We discuss transmission line inductor, single coil inductor, 2.5-turn inductor and multi-layer inductor, which can be used in millimeter-wave circuits. We present a multi-layer inductor implemented in 0.13 μm one-poly and seven-metal (1P7M) BiCMOS SiGe process and propose a modified double-π model for on-chip multi-layer inductor. Self-resonance frequency (SRF) beyond 100 GHz were obtained based on the measurement results, demonstrating that the multi-layer inductor can be used for millimeter-wave applications with compact size and high inductance density.

articleTitle: A novel 245 GHz 4thindex push-push VCO
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A novel 245 GHz 4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup>index harmonicpush-push VCO is presented in IHP SiGe: C BiCMOS technology with f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</sub> and f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</sub> of 300 and 500 GHz respectively. The VCO utilizes the 4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup>harmonic index in the push-push oscillating core to obtain 245 GHz signals. The VCO comprises of a 4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup>harmonic oscillating core with 1/64 divider and a 245 GHz common base (CB) LNA buffer stage. The output power of the VCO reaches -18 dBmat 251 GHz with a phase noise of -86 dBc/Hz at 1 MHz offset frequency. The VCO has a tuning range of 18 GHz, occupies an area of 0.45 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and dissipates 179 mW with divider, or 95 mW without divider.

articleTitle: A 28-GHz 256-QAM Power Amplifier with Weakly-Coupled Transformers in 65-nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents a 28-GHz three-stage pseudodifferential neutralized power amplifier (PA) for 5G applications. A fully-coupled transformer is chosen as the output matching network to reduce loss and improve efficiency, while weakly-coupled transformers are adopted as the input and inter-stage matching networks to extend bandwidth. An optimization method is proposed to ensure power performance while maintaining bandwidth. Implemented in 65-nm CMOS technology at 1-V supply, the prototype delivers a saturated output power of 12.7 dBm with a peak PAE of 29.5%. It offers a small signal gain of 23.7 dB with 3-dB bandwidth from 25.9 GHz to 33.1 GHz. The chip occupies a core area of 0.82×0.24 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A Novel Dual-Band Bandpass Filter based on Substrate Integrated Coaxial Line
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, a novel dual-band bandpass filter based on the technology of substrate integrated coaxial line (SICL) is proposed. The proposed bandpass filter which can be realized in standard printed circuit boards (PCB)-exhibits the advantages of compact size, low cost, high selectivity low profile and easy integration with other planar circuits in the future. Since substrate integrated coaxial line (SICL) is a kind of enclosed structure, the filter using this technology will reduce the radiation loss effectively. The simulated results show that the proposed bandpass filter based on SLCL promises to be useful in the design of future microwave and millimeter wave circuits and systems.

articleTitle: Fully Implantable Miniature RF Sensor for Continuous Glucose Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this work, implantable biosensor for continuous monitoring of blood sugar level using miniature microwave sensor is presented. Contrary to the conventional in vivo sensors to measure blood sugar level directly from blood, the present bio implant sensor measures sugar level in interstitial fluid. The perdition accuracy can be significantly improved based on our regression and correlation model with a shorter calibration time. The RF sensor is operating in industrial scientific medical (ISM) band and compatible with existing technology in terms of hardware and software architecture.

articleTitle: A Compact Bandpass Filter with Wide Stopband and Two Finite Transmission Zeros
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A compact bandpass filter with wide stopband and two finite transmission zeros is proposed in this paper. By means of the coupling control, two finite transmission zeros can be introduced in the combline filter response. Four transmission zeros on the upper stopband can be created by the source/load coupling and spurlines etched on the transmission lines, which can achieve wide stopband of the filter. The working center frequency and relative bandwidth of the designed filter are respectively 3.47 GHz and 4.3%. The measured return loss and insertion loss of this filter are better than 16.7 dB and less than 0.9 dB in the range of 3.39 GHz to 3.54 GHz, respectively. The upper stopband is extended up to 3.77f0 with an insertion loss larger than 19 dB.

articleTitle: Radome Design with Improved Aerodynamics and Radiation for Smart Antennas in Automotive Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: More applications are using wireless communication, where the radomes become more important as they are essential in the performance of antennas as well as protect antennas from environmental conditions. The focus in this study is to design a radome for a customized smart antenna such that the attenuation of antenna signal and the increase in drag coefficient of vehicle are minimized. This paper presents a novel method of radome design and the simulation results demonstrate that the drag coefficient of the vehicle is slightly increased by less than 2% while the loss to the signal strength is less than 0.5 dB.

articleTitle: A Direct Matching Network Synthesization Technique Designed for Class-J Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, a novel direct matching network (MN) synthesization method is presented to design a broadband class-J PA. By straightforwardly optimize the characteristic impedance (physical width) and electrical length (physical length) of each distributed element in a preselected configuration, the proposed method improves design flexibility and matching effects. A novel target function (TF) indicating the degree of proximity for the realized impedance to the optimal transistor impedance is proposed. The designed class-J PA using the proposed method shows a broadband performance of greater than 62% PAE, the gain of more than 10.8 dB and almost 40 dBm output power with a 2.5-3.8 GHz (41.3%) bandwidth.

articleTitle: Passive Components Design Based on LTCC Technology for Front-End Module in Ka-Band
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents a Ka-band front-end frequency conversion module. In the passive component design, a RF filter with the substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) structure is introduced. It can be completely buried in the LTCC substrate, and two transmission zero points are added to make it have high frequency selection characteristics. A probe-like structure is used to transmit the signal from the top-layer to the SIW cavity. The power divider with a stripline structure is used to connect the frequency conversion module to the multi-channel transceiver component. The surface-mounted GaAs thin film resistor connect to the power divider through a vertical metal via. These two types of passive structures are tested by a probe station. Finally, this paper analyzes the cause of the difference between the measured results and the simulation results.

articleTitle: Wideband Bandpass Filters Using Half-Mode Corrugated Substrate Integrated Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A wideband bandpass filter is proposed in this paper, the filter combine half-mode corrugated substrate integrated waveguide (HMCSIW) with improved dumbbell defected ground structures (DGSs). The HMCSIW technique can operate similarly with the traditional half-mode substrate integrated waveguide (HMSIW). Differently, it provides a completely floating conductor without metallic via holes. Combining two technologies together, a design of HMCSIW wideband bandpass filter (BPF) is proposed in the paper. The presented BPFs can operate in a wide band without a short circuit between different metal layers and will be widely used in integration with other RF circuits.

articleTitle: Support Vector Regression Based Behavioral Model for Load Mismatched PAs
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A new double-input double-output (DIDO) power amplifier (PA) behavioral model, which takes into account output load termination mismatches, is presented in this paper. The support vector regression (SVR) methodology, from the field of machine learning, is utilized to build this new model. The model is intended for the system-level simulation of amplifier chains subjected to wideband modulated signals. It is validated by comparing the predicted and measured data of a 15 W Gallium Nitride (GaN) based PA under a wide range of voltage standing wave ratios (VSWR). Compared with the conventional memory polynomial (MP) based DIDO models, the obtained results from the new model demonstrate the improved prediction capabilities.

articleTitle: A 14-GHz 8-bit Direct Digital Synthesizer in InP DHBT Technology
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper describes a 14-GHz 8-bit direct digital synthesizer(DDS)which is implemented using a 0.7-μm InP double hetero-junction bipolar transistor (DHBT) process. The DDS presented uses a sin-weighted nonlinear DAC to achieve a phase-to-amplitude ROM-less architecture which can make the best of speed advantage of the InP DHBT process for medium to large scale mixed signal integrated circuits. A simplified pipelined phase accumulator is used to reduce power consumption. The average value of SFDR of the output signal of the DDS in the Nyquist bandwidth is -24.8 dBc. The circuit integrates 2122 transistors, consumes a power of 2.4-W, and has a Figure of Merit (FOM) of 5.83GHz/W.

articleTitle: A 4.9-GHz GaN MMIC Doherty Power Amplifier for 5G Application
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: -This paper presents the simulation result of a 4.9-GHz GaN MMIC Doherty Power Amplifier for 5G Application using a 0.25-μm gallium nitride (GaN)-HEMT process. According to the simulation results, a saturated power of 40 dBm-40.3 dBm, a saturated drain efficiency (DE) of 60%-63%, and a 6-dB back-off DE of 51%-53% are achieved from 4.8 GHz to 5 GHz. When driven by a 100MHz orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) signal with 6.1 dB peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR), an adjacent channel leakage ratio (ACLR) of -29 dBc with a DE of 50% was achieved at an average power of 34 dBm. After a digital predistortion process, the ACLR was improved to -46 dBc.

articleTitle: One-Chip CMOS Terahertz Transceiver
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In the future, terahertz communication using the 300 GHz band has attracted attention from the expectation that the unallocated frequency band exceeding 275 GHz will be available. In terahertz band communication using ultrahigh frequency, compound semiconductors having excellent high frequency performance have been used in previous researches. Nevertheless, research on wireless transceivers using silicon integrated circuits, in particular CMOS integrated circuits, is increasing in this 300 GHz band. This article outlines one-chip terahertz transceiver technology using mass-produced silicon integrated circuits, its applications, and the future.

articleTitle: A 32.2-GHz Full Adder in InP DHBT Technology
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: An ultra-high speed 1bit full adder based on indium phosphide (InP) double heterojunction bipolar transistor (DHBT) technology is presented. The synchronous latch is combined with adding operation to improve the calculation speed. A single-level parallel-gated circuit is designed using majority decision algorithm to reduce the power consumption. Measurement results show that the maximum clock frequency of the full adder is 32.2-GHz, and the overall power consumption is 350mW.

articleTitle: CMOS Transceiver Pixels for Terahertz Imaging
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Pixels integrating a transmitter and a coherent receiver in an area of half-wavelength square are proposed for terahertz active imaging. 300- and 427-GHz transceiver pixels are demonstrated using a 65-nm CMOS process. The 300-GHz pixel employs a push-push stacked cross-coupled VCO, which doubles as a transmitter and an LO, and a pair of diode-connected NMOS transistors for mixing. The pixel occupies an area of 450×580µm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and provides −21.3-dBm total radiated power and −79.5-dBm sensitivity for a 1-kHz noise bandwidth at 260GHz. The 426-GHz pixel using a star-type triple-push Colpitts oscillator works as a transmitter and a self-oscillating mixer. The pixel occupies an area of 380×470µm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The radiated power is −17.9 dBm and the sensitivity is −89.6 dBm for a 1-kHz noise bandwidth. Link-budget analyses suggest that camera-like reflection-mode imaging of targets 5m away should be possible using the pixel and a 4.6cm×4.6cm reflector.

articleTitle: A Novel PCB design Technique for Dual-polarized 5G Phased Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A 2X4 dual polarized co-axial fed patch antenna array is designed on an eight Layer PCB with a gain of 14.0 dBi and a bandwidth of 1 GHz for 5G Local Multipoint Distribution Service (LMDS) band operation. A specialized PCB design process is adopted to accommodate two exclusive zones, housing the mm-wave transceiver and the digital section uniquely. To boost the data rate, polarization diversity is utilized and power from(to) two polarization ports are combined in the PCB and then fed to the PA(LNA) interface in an LTCC Package. The phased array design is further supported with beam forming simulations.

articleTitle: Stability Evaluation of a Broadband Multi-Stage Low Noise Amplifier using Nonlinear Analysis
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, the stability evaluation of a broadband multi-stage low noise amplifier (LNA) is presented using nonlinear analysis. The demonstrated LNA consists of three common-source stages with resistance-capacitance feedback, and it is implemented in 0.15-μm GaAs pHEMT process. The linear inter-stage stability analysis and the nonlinear stability analysis are employed to predict the occurrence of low-frequency and microwave oscillations. The simulated results are demonstrated to eliminate instabilities in the broadband multi-stage LNA, especially for the low- and high-frequency bands. Moreover, the LNA features a measured 3-dB bandwidth from 4 to 16 GHz, a maximum small-signal gain of 28 dB, a minimum noise figure of 2 dB. The measured output 1-dB compression point is higher than -3 dBm. The demonstrated method for stability is suitable for the microwave linear and nonlinear circuits.

articleTitle: A 60GHz Compact Wideband Differential Hybrid Based on Folded Transformer
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents a 60 GHz wideband differential lumped-element hybrid based on folded transformer. With a 65nm CMOS process, the hybrid utilizes a coplanar folded transformer to achieve an enhanced coupling factor, resulting in competitive results with low loss, differential wideband operation, and compact size at 60 GHz band. Simulations demonstrate a maximum differential quadrature outputs phase error within ± 2° from 42 to 85 GHz, maximum magnitude mismatch within ± 1 dB from 48 to 76 GHz, and a worst-case image rejection ratio of 30 dB from 52 to 73 GHz, a passive loss of 2.28 dB at 60 GHz. This hybrid occupies a core area of 0.015 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: 56Gbaud Linear PAM4 Transimepedance Amplifier and VCSEL Driver in 55nm BiCMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A linear 56Gbaud PAM4 transimpedance amplifier (TIA) and a VCSEL-based driver are presented in this paper. It can meet the requirements of emerging 400G Ethernet. The equalizer technique is both adopted in TIA and driver to extend bandwidth. The AGC in TIA can provide 33.4dB gain control range and it accommodates input currents from 35uApp up to 2 mApp. To improve its linearity, the driver adopts feedforward equalizer(FFE) to decrease its group delay peak-peak value. By using advanced SiGe BiCMOS technology, the operating bits rates of each channel in TIA and driver can be up to 112Gbps.

articleTitle: Design of a Three-cavity Dual-mode Bandpass SIW Filter
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A three-cavity dual-mode bandpass substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) filter is proposed in this paper. Two dual-mode isosceles triangle cavities with one port on the waist, the other port on the base and a dual-mode isosceles triangle cavity with two ports on the waist of the triangle cavities upper surface are used as basic elements. By cascading three basic elements and adding metallic via-holes between coupling windows, a compact and more wider bandpass three-cavity dual-mode SIW filter is realized. Additionally, S parameter and Z parameter fit in with theoretical analysis. Finally, a 10.11% fractional bandwidth filter is achieved.

articleTitle: Design of Bandpass Filter Based on Folded Multimode Resonator
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents a bandpass filter based on microstrip lines which are folded to make a multimode triangular shape resonator operating in the frequency range of 2.35-2.41GHz. The folded microstrip ring structure was able to produce more than one passband by adjusting the coupling between feedlines and folded microstrip line resonator, and one passband was used here. Proposed filter is designed, simulated and measured. The results show that the insertion loss is around 2.3dB within a 3dB bandwidth of 130MHz.

articleTitle: Characterization of Electromagnetic Nonlinearities of RFI/EMI Gasket: A Microstrip Based Approach
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: The knowledge of the electromagnetic nonlinearities of materials is of paramount importance for a wide variety of application. RFI/EMI shielding gasket is comparatively a new material used in this domain, and its electromagnetic nonlinearities are not very renowned. This research focused to develop a microstrip-based technique to study the electromagnetic nonlinearities of RFI shielding gaskets, which involved third & fifth-order passive intermodulation (PIM), and second & third-order harmonic distortion (HD). A bit of nickel and two types of gaskets were use as material-under-test (MUT) at 700MHz frequency band. The output of this research might help in the material selection for wide variety of applications.

articleTitle: A Compact Bandpass Filter Using Quarter-Mode Substrate Integrated Waveguide and Composite Right/Left-Handed Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this letter, a compact bandpass filter based on an interdigital fingers resonator and a quarter-mode substrate integrated waveguide (QMSIW) resonator is proposed. The center frequency of the resonator structure which is loaded with the composite right/left-handed (CRLH) transmission lines is below the characteristic frequency of the QMSIW resonator. And three transmission zero points (TZs) are introduced to improve the out-of-band rejection of the passband. In addition, a rectangular slot is introduced into the filter to improve the passband performance and further reduce the filter size. A compact CRLH-QMSIW filter is designed and fabricated. The test result shows a good agreement between the measurement and simulation.

articleTitle: A 180-nm CMOS 100MHz-1.2GHz Software-Defined Transceiver with Integrated Pre-Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: As a method to realize multi-mode terminal for mobile and wireless communication standards, software-defined radio (SDR) has attracted intensive studies. A wideband wireless transceiver is designed in a 180-nm CMOS process for SDR, which can operate over a frequency range from 100MHz to 1.2GHz. The wideband RF front-end includes a low noise amplifier (LNA), a power amplifier (PA), mixers, a frequency synthesizer, a programmable intermediate frequency band pass filter (BPF) and a variable gain amplifier (VGA). The noise figure (NF) of the receiver is 2.2-3.9 dB thanks to the wideband LNA with noise cancellation. The transmitter can achieve a saturation power of more than 16.8 dBm over the operating frequency range. The overall power consumption for the whole system is more than 492mW with a power supply of 1.8 V.

articleTitle: Continuous Frequency-Sweep Covering Normal Direction Using Spoof Plasmonic Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Spoof surface plasmon polaritons are mimicing surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) modes at microwave or terahertz frequencies based on periodic metamaterial. The SPP mode has been widely used in novel transmission waveguides and functional devices, due to its unique properties of great confinement, shorter operating wavelength, low loss, and ability in flexible transmission. A frequency-sweep radiation based on complementary SSPP transmission line is proposed, in which the frequency-scanning on both sides of the transmission line is achieved. Additional array of circular patches is introduced to overcome the disadvantage of low-radiation-efficiency in the normal direction. Leaky-wave radiation within wide-range from backward direction to forward direction is achieved.

articleTitle: Compact design of complementary spoof surface plasmon polaritons transmission line
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Novel miniaturized design of complementary spoof surface plasmon polaritons transmission line (CSSPP-TL) is proposed in microwave frequency. It is composed of complementary corrugated metallic strip and interdigital structures (ISs). The proposed CSSPP-TL features small linewidth, flexible dispersion control, and highly selective filtering performance. Simulated results show that the proposed CSSPP-TL has low insertion loss and high transmission efficiency. The dispersion properties of CSSPP with interdigital structures are studied. The cutoff frequency of the design is decreased by 50%, compared to that of conventional CSSPP transmission line, which indicate that, by introducing extra ISs, a smaller propagating wavelength and a tighter electric field confinement is realized, ensuring reliable applications in miniaturized plasmonic devices and low-interference SPPs circuits.

articleTitle: Multi-Level Modulation for High-Speed Wireless and Wireline Transceivers
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Multi-level modulations are important techniques to achieve high data rate in wireless transceivers which bandwidth is limited by regulations. In wireline transceivers, data rate has been increased by expanding the bandwidth which is not limited by regulations. However, it is difficult to expand the bandwidth anymore for technical issues and multi-level modulations are introduced in wireline transceivers. In this paper, multi-level modulation examples used in wireless and wireline transceivers are presented.

articleTitle: A Passive Equalizer Design for On-Interposer Differential Interconnects in 2.5D/3D ICs
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper introduce a passive equalizer for compensating the frequency characteristics of on-interposer differential interconnects in TSV-based 3-D ICs. To facilitate the design of the equalizer, we develop a simplified odd-mode circuit model, which only consists of four elements. The simplified model can capture the electrical performance of the differential interconnects quickly and accurately up to 20 GHz. Then, the equalizer parameters are designed by using the time-domain inter-symbol interference (ISI) cancellation method, and then used for extracting the geometrical parameters. The functionality of the passive equalizer is validated in both frequency- and time-domain.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Identification of ADC in Transceiver based on Higher-Order-Statistic
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper aims at identifying the nonlinearity of ADC in transceivers which consists ADC and DAC. ADC is considered as "black-box", a two-step adaptive algorithm is proposed based on normalized kurtosis of input and output signal. Kurtosis is the 4th order Statistic which owns many impotent features in identifying or calibrating weak nonlinear systems. Simulation result shows that the nonlinearity of ADC could be identified accurately, thus it could be further used in calibrating ADC to improve its SFDR.
